title: Discere deck recipe
description: How scripts/build_deck.py builds one catalog deck from observation data: recipes/<base>.json becomes data/decks/<base>.json and the report recipes/<base>.report.md. The deck texts and learning settings use the definitions of deck.schema.json. Relative paths are relative to the recipe file. Without region, the deck is worldwide.

$schema.description: Reference to this schema, so editors complete and check while writing.

deck.description: What the deck says about itself; written to the deck as given. imageUrl and createdBy, if missing here, keep the value of an existing deck file.

order.description: The source whose counts rank the species. inat: iNaturalist research-grade observations, for seas. gbif: GBIF occurrences in a country, for inland waters. reef: the sighting frequency (SF%) of a REEF CSV export, where REEF has survey data.

csv.description: Path to the REEF CSV export.

region.description: The region, in the terms of each source; each may name several areas. Only the sources given here are asked; OBIS and the distribution data only confirm occurrence. Leave the whole region out for a worldwide deck (e.g. a group of animals): iNaturalist then counts worldwide, and only the order source and the guides confirm occurrence. With a region and order inat, region.inat is required, so a region never silently means worldwide.

inat.description: iNaturalist places, counted together in one query without counting an observation twice, or a rectangle for seas without fitting places.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, e.g. CH; the occurrences of all of them count together.

obis.description: Sea areas, asked together as one MULTIPOLYGON, so a record in two overlapping areas counts once.

name.description: Name of the area, for the report.

wkt.description: The area as WKT POLYGON or MULTIPOLYGON, longitude before latitude.

fishbase.description: FishBase/SeaLifeBase distribution regions as the reference DB keys them (taxonomy_distribution_regions.region_key): a FishBase country code, e.g. 756 for Switzerland or 840B for a part of a country FishBase lists on its own, or a subregion, e.g. 840:US-FL for Florida.

taxa.description: Which organisms, in the IDs of each source asked: required for an iNaturalist or GBIF order and for OBIS; a REEF CSV needs none.

inat.description: iNaturalist taxon IDs, e.g. 47178 ray-finned fishes, 47273 sharks and rays, 49232 lampreys (not 47237, which is the angelfish family).

obis.description: WoRMS taxon IDs, e.g. 10194 Actinopteri, 10193 Elasmobranchii.

gbif.description: The GBIF phylum whose orders are searched; the orders the reference DB knows as FishBase orders are kept, since the GBIF backbone gives the ray-finned fishes no class.

filters.description: Conditions a candidate from the order source has to meet; an unknown value never excludes. Highlights are not filtered.

water.description: salt: the FishBase/SeaLifeBase flag Saltwater is set (brackish alone is not enough); fresh: Fresh is set; any: no condition. A species with all three flags at 0 counts as unknown.

minCount.description: Minimum count in the order source: observations, or SF% for REEF.

diveDepthLimitM.description: Leaves out species whose shallowest depth lies below this many meters.

minLengthCm.description: Leaves out species whose maximum length is below this many centimeters.

levelSizes.description: Number of species per level, from level 1; level 1 also holds the highlights on top of its size.

highlights.description: Species worth knowing in the region even if rare, picked by hand; they go on level 1. Each needs evidence in the region (order source, OBIS, distribution data or a guide), or it stays out and the run fails.

guides.description: Species lists of field guides, one scientific name per line. They confirm occurrence and are compared with the deck in the report; they never filter.

url.description: Where the list comes from; listed in the deck's sources.
